CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: In Carnatic music, which term refers to the melodic framework that shapes a composition?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: A raga provides the melodic framework and characteristic note movements.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Which term describes the ascending movement of notes in a raga?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Arohana describes ascending note movement.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Which term describes the descending movement of notes in a raga?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Avarohana describes descending note movement.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What are the seven basic swara names in Carnatic music?
options: Sa, Ri, Ga, Ma, Pa, Da, Ni
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: The seven basic swaras are Sa, Ri, Ga, Ma, Pa, Da and Ni.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is the role of the tonic or adhara shadja?
options: It provides the pitch reference for the performance
It names the final lyric stanza
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: The tonic gives the singer a stable pitch reference.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is a gamaka?
options: A characteristic melodic ornament or pitch movement
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Gamakas are important melodic ornaments in Carnatic music.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is a raga's characteristic phrase or usage often called?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Prayoga refers to characteristic usage or phrase in a raga.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What does 'manodharma' mean in Carnatic music?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Manodharma is the creative improvisational aspect of performance.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: How many parent ragas are in the standard melakarta system?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: The standard melakarta system has 72 parent ragas.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is a janya raga?
options: A raga derived from a melakarta parent raga
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Janya ragas are derived from parent melakarta ragas.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Which raga is widely used for foundational lessons in many Carnatic music schools?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Mayamalavagowla is commonly used for foundational lessons, though practice varies.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Which raga is commonly described as pentatonic in both ascent and descent?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Mohanam is a well-known five-note raga in ascent and descent.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Which swara sequence is commonly associated with Shankarabharanam?
options: Sa Ri1 Ga2 Ma1 Pa Da1 Ni2 Sa
Sa Ri2 Ga2 Ma2 Pa Da2 Ni2 Sa
Sa Ri2 Ga3 Ma1 Pa Da2 Ni3 Sa
Sa Ga3 Ma1 Da2 Ni3 Sa
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: This is the commonly taught ascending scale of Shankarabharanam.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is the principal purpose of learning a raga's arohana and avarohana?
options: To understand its basic ascending and descending note patterns
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: These patterns help outline a raga's basic note structure.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Why are characteristic phrases important when identifying a raga?
options: They replace the need for pitch
They specify the concert ticket price
They help express the raga's distinctive melodic identity
They determine the language of every lyric
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Characteristic phrases can be essential to raga identity beyond a simple scale.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is alapana?
options: Free melodic exploration of a raga, generally without a fixed tala cycle
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Alapana develops a raga's melodic possibilities without a fixed tala cycle.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is neraval?
options: Improvisation based on a selected line of a composition
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Neraval develops melodic and rhythmic variations around a chosen line.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What are kalpana swarams?
options: Improvised passages sung using swara syllables
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Kalpana swarams are improvised note passages.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: In a Ragam-Tanam-Pallavi presentation, what does the ragam section mainly explore?
options: Only the lyrics of the charanam
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: The ragam section develops the raga's melodic character.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is a common melodic feature of tanam?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Tanam is a rhythmic-melodic improvisational section.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is the purpose of practicing a raga slowly before increasing speed?
options: To improve pitch accuracy and clarity of phrases
To change the raga into another one
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Slow practice helps develop accuracy before faster execution.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is a kriti?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: A kriti is a major compositional form in Carnatic music.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Which section of a typical kriti often serves as its opening refrain?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Pallavi is commonly the opening or refrain section.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is a sangati in a kriti?
options: A melodic variation of a line
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Sangatis are melodic variations developed for a composition line.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is the role of sahitya in a vocal composition?
options: It is the lyric or textual content
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Sahitya refers to the lyrics or text.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is a varnam often used to develop?
options: Melodic familiarity, voice control, and rhythmic accuracy
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Varnams are important for learning and performance technique.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Which composer's compositions are predominantly in Telugu?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Many of Tyagaraja's compositions are in Telugu.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Which composer is particularly associated with many Sanskrit compositions?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Many of Dikshitar's compositions are in Sanskrit.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Which composer is especially associated with compositions praising Goddess Kamakshi?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Syama Sastri is especially known for compositions on Goddess Kamakshi.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Which composer is traditionally called the Pitamaha of Carnatic music?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Purandara Dasa is traditionally regarded as a foundational teacher of Carnatic music.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Which instrument commonly provides the continuous drone in Carnatic vocal music?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: The tambura provides the continuous pitch drone.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is the common melodic role of the violin in a Carnatic vocal concert?
options: It accompanies and responds to the vocalist
It is used only to announce the raga
It replaces the drone in every concert
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: The violin commonly follows and responds to the vocalist's melodic phrases.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Which term refers to keeping the voice aligned with the pitch reference?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Sruti shuddham refers to accurate pitch alignment.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is the benefit of listening for gamakas in a raga performance?
options: It helps recognize characteristic melodic expression
It tells the exact ticket price
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Gamakas can be central to a raga's characteristic expression.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Why should a student listen to several renditions of the same raga?
options: To learn its characteristic phrases and interpretive possibilities
To prove every rendition must be identical
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Multiple renditions can reveal both raga grammar and individual interpretation.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is a useful first step when trying to identify an unfamiliar raga by ear?
options: Guess only from the singer's costume
Listen for its characteristic phrases and note movements
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Characteristic phrases and note movements are useful clues.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is the purpose of sarali varisai?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Sarali varisai introduces basic note patterns.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What do janta varisai exercises emphasize?
options: Only the final verse of a kriti
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Janta varisai helps practise repeated notes and control.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is the main focus of alankaram exercises?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Alankaram exercises combine note patterns with tala.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Why should a student practise a phrase with a shruti drone?
options: To strengthen pitch alignment and tonal awareness
To make every raga sound identical
To remove the need for rhythm
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: A drone supports tonal reference and pitch awareness.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is a healthy approach to developing melodic range?
options: Extend range gradually without forcing the voice
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Gradual practice reduces unnecessary strain.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What should a vocalist do if singing causes persistent pain or hoarseness?
options: Stop forcing the voice and seek qualified advice if it persists
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Persistent pain or hoarseness should not be ignored.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Who composed the Pancharatna Kritis?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: The Pancharatna Kritis are five celebrated compositions of Tyagaraja.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Who composed 'Vatapi Ganapatim' in the commonly accepted attribution?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: 'Vatapi Ganapatim' is attributed to Muthuswami Dikshitar.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Which raga is commonly associated with 'Vatapi Ganapatim'?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: 'Vatapi Ganapatim' is commonly rendered in Hamsadhwani.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Which raga is associated with Tyagaraja's 'Endaro Mahanubhavulu'?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: 'Endaro Mahanubhavulu' is a Pancharatna kriti in Sri raga.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Which composer is associated with the composition 'Kurai Ondrum Illai'?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: 'Kurai Ondrum Illai' is attributed to C. Rajagopalachari.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What does a raga's melodic identity depend on besides its scale?
options: Characteristic phrases, note treatment, and gamakas
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Raga identity often depends on characteristic phrases and note treatment, not merely scale.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Which term refers to the ascent and descent patterns of a raga?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Arohana and avarohana describe ascending and descending note patterns.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is the broad purpose of a raga alapana in a concert?
options: To recite the full lyrics only
To reveal the raga's character through melodic development
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Alapana develops the raga's character through melodic exploration.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What does 'raga bhava' refer to?
options: The expressive character or mood conveyed by a raga
The physical size of a stage
The count of beats in a tala
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Raga bhava refers to the expressive character associated with a raga.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is a common purpose of singing swara passages after a composition line?
options: To demonstrate melodic improvisation and note control
To mark the concert's end every time
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Swara passages can demonstrate melodic improvisation and control.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Which is the most appropriate way to compare two ragas with similar scales?
options: Compare characteristic phrases and how notes are treated
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Characteristic phrasing and note treatment can distinguish ragas with similar scales.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is meant by a raga's 'prayoga' in practical learning?
options: A characteristic way notes are used in phrases
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Prayoga concerns characteristic note usage and phrases.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Why is it useful to sing a raga's phrases rather than only its scale?
options: A scale always contains every musical detail
Phrases help capture the raga's distinctive grammar and expression
It eliminates the need for pitch accuracy
Phrases are unrelated to raga identity
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: A scale alone may not express all the defining features of a raga.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Which statement best describes Carnatic melodic improvisation?
options: It must use only one note
It is creative but guided by the raga's grammar and tradition
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Improvisation allows creativity within the raga's musical grammar.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Which part of a raga performance is generally not tied to a fixed tala cycle?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Alapana is generally presented without a fixed tala cycle.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is the role of a tonic drone when learning a new raga?
options: It provides a stable tonal centre for singing and listening
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: A tonic drone anchors the pitch reference.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Which statement about gamakas is most accurate?
options: Every gamaka is identical in every raga
Their use and shape can vary with the raga and musical context
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Gamakas are context-sensitive and contribute to melodic identity.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Which skill helps a singer reproduce a melodic phrase accurately after hearing it?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Focused listening and repetition build melodic memory.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What does 'sangati' practice help a student understand?
options: How a composition line can be elaborated melodically
How to replace tala with silence
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Sangatis demonstrate melodic elaboration of a composition line.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is the main melodic goal of practising with a teacher's demonstrated phrases?
options: To learn correct raga phrasing and note treatment
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: A teacher's phrasing can help transmit nuanced raga grammar.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Which approach best supports learning a new kriti melodically?
options: Sing it at top speed immediately
Learn phrase by phrase, maintain pitch, and understand the raga
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Phrase-by-phrase learning supports accuracy and understanding.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is the key distinction between a composition's melody and its tala?
options: Melody organizes pitches and phrases; tala organizes rhythmic time
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Melody and tala are distinct but coordinated aspects of music.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What does 'pitch accuracy' mean in vocal practice?
options: Singing notes in tune with the intended pitch reference
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Pitch accuracy means matching the intended notes and tonal reference.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Why should a singer avoid forcing gamakas before learning their shape?
options: It removes the need for a drone
It can create strain and inaccurate melodic treatment
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Gamakas should be learned carefully to preserve accuracy and vocal comfort.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is a useful way to internalize a raga's melodic character?
options: Listen, sing characteristic phrases, and practise them with a stable sruti
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Listening and phrase practice with a stable pitch reference reinforce raga understanding.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What does 'melodic contour' mean?
options: The number of people in a concert
The shape or direction of a musical line
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Melodic contour describes how a musical line rises, falls, or moves.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Which term most directly describes a sequence of notes sung as musical syllables such as Sa and Ri?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: A swara passage uses note syllables rather than lyric text.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What should a student do when two raga phrases sound similar at first?
options: Compare the note movements, gamakas, and characteristic usage carefully
Choose based on the concert venue
Assume the ragas are the same
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Careful comparison of phrases and note treatment helps distinguish similar-sounding ragas.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is the main purpose of a melodic exercise in multiple speeds?
options: To maintain clarity and pitch accuracy as tempo changes
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Multiple-speed practice develops control while preserving clarity.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Which factor most directly helps maintain a consistent tonic while practising?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: A steady shruti reference helps maintain tonic alignment.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: What is the best description of a raga's 'grammar'?
options: Only the spelling of the raga name
Conventions governing characteristic note use, phrases, and melodic movement
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Raga grammar includes characteristic note use and melodic conventions.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Why is melody-focused listening useful for a Carnatic vocalist?
options: It removes the need to practise
It develops awareness of raga phrases, intonation, and expressive detail
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: Melody-focused listening supports raga and intonation awareness.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Choose the correct answer: In Carnatic music, which term refers to the melodic framework that shapes a composition?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: A raga provides the melodic framework and characteristic note movements.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Carnatic melodic practice: In Carnatic music, which term refers to the melodic framework that shapes a composition?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: A raga provides the melodic framework and characteristic note movements.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.q: Which option best answers this question: In Carnatic music, which term refers to the melodic framework that shapes a composition?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Melodic.why: A raga provides the melodic framework and characteristic note movements.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: Which instrument is regarded as the principal percussion instrument in many Carnatic concerts?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: The mridangam is the principal percussion instrument in many Carnatic performances.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: Which Carnatic percussion instrument is made from a clay pot?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: The ghatam is a clay-pot percussion instrument.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: Which instrument is a small frame drum commonly used in Carnatic music?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: The kanjira is a small frame drum used in Carnatic percussion.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: Which instrument is played by vibrating a metal tongue held near the mouth?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: The morsing is a jaw harp used in Carnatic percussion.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What is the main role of percussion in a Carnatic vocal concert?
options: To support and develop the rhythmic framework
To set the tonic pitch only
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Percussion supports tala and contributes rhythmic interaction.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What does 'tala' refer to in Carnatic music?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Tala organizes musical time in a repeating rhythmic framework.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What does 'laya' mean?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Laya refers to tempo or temporal flow.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What is an 'akshara' in tala counting broadly associated with?
options: A counted unit in the rhythmic cycle
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Akshara is a counted unit in tala.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: Which is one of the seven basic talas in the Carnatic system?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Dhruva is one of the seven basic Carnatic tala families.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: Which tala is commonly counted as eight aksharas in its standard chatusra-jati form?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Chatusra-jati Adi tala is commonly counted as eight aksharas.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What are the three principal tala angas commonly taught in Carnatic theory?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: The main angas are laghu, drutam, and anudrutam.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What determines the count of a laghu?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: The jati determines the laghu's count.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What is a common hand action used to mark tala?
options: Clapping and finger counts or waves
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Tala is marked with prescribed actions such as claps, finger counts, and waves.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What is the usual akshara count for chatusra-jati Adi tala?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: The standard cycle is counted as eight aksharas.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What does 'jati' determine in the tala anga system?
options: The number of counts in a laghu
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Jati specifies the laghu count.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What is a 'korvai' commonly understood as?
options: A structured rhythmic phrase or sequence
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: A korvai is a structured rhythmic pattern, often used as a cadence.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What is a 'mora' in Carnatic rhythmic practice?
options: A rhythmic phrase structured around a repeated pattern, often threefold
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: A mora is a patterned rhythmic phrase, often organized in a three-part structure.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What does 'nadai' or 'gati' describe in rhythmic practice?
options: The subdivision or gait of the beat
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Nadai/gati concerns how the beat is subdivided.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: Which term describes a rhythmic pattern played in a different subdivision from the main one?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: A nadai change alters the subdivision or gait.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What is a 'solkattu' or 'konnakol' syllable pattern used for?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Solkattu and konnakol use spoken syllables to represent rhythm.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: Which is a common set of spoken rhythmic syllables in Carnatic practice?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Syllables such as tha, dhin, thom, and nam are used in rhythmic practice.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What is the purpose of practising rhythmic patterns with a metronome or tala app?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: A metronome or tala app can support steady timing practice.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What does 'eduppu' refer to in a composition?
options: The point where the music begins relative to the tala cycle
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Eduppu is the entry point of a musical phrase in relation to the tala.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What is 'arudi' often associated with in a composition?
options: A point of emphasis or structural landing
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Arudi is a structurally important point of emphasis in some compositions.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What is a 'tani avartanam'?
options: A percussion solo within a tala cycle
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Tani avartanam is the percussion solo segment in a Carnatic concert.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: Which instrument most commonly leads the tani avartanam in a standard Carnatic concert?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: The mridangam commonly leads the percussion solo, with other percussionists participating.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What is an important skill for a percussion accompanist?
options: Listening and responding to the main artist while maintaining tala
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Good accompaniment requires rhythmic steadiness and attentive musical interaction.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What does 'sarvalaghu' broadly describe in mridangam playing?
options: A flowing, relatively even rhythmic accompaniment style
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Sarvalaghu refers broadly to a flowing accompaniment approach.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What is a 'chapu tala' commonly associated with?
options: A tala with characteristic asymmetric groupings
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Chapu talas often use asymmetric rhythmic groupings.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: Which of these is commonly known as a chapu tala?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Misra Chapu is a commonly used chapu tala.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What is a key purpose of a percussion korvai near the end of a solo?
options: To create a planned rhythmic conclusion aligned with the tala
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: A korvai often builds toward a rhythmic landing on the tala cycle.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: Why must a percussionist know the composition's eduppu?
options: To coordinate rhythmic phrases with the music's entry point
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Knowing the eduppu helps the accompanist align patterns with the composition.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: Which instrument is played with the fingers and palms on a double-headed drum?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: The mridangam is a double-headed drum played with hands and fingers.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What is one common technique used to produce sound on a ghatam?
options: Striking different areas of the pot with fingers and palms
Bowing the rim with a violin bow
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Ghatam players use fingers, palms, and different pot areas to create varied tones.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: How is the kanjira generally played?
options: By striking and controlling the frame drum with the hand
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: The kanjira is played by hand, with techniques that control tone and resonance.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What is the morsing's basic sound-producing method?
options: A vibrating tongue is plucked while the instrument is held near the mouth
A drumhead is struck with sticks
Air is blown through a reed
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: The morsing is a jaw harp with a vibrating tongue.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: Why is hand technique important for a mridangam player?
options: It affects tone quality, clarity, and rhythmic articulation
It removes the need to practise tala
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Hand technique affects the tone and articulation of strokes.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What is a useful beginner approach to learning percussion strokes?
options: Learn slowly with correct technique before increasing speed
Play as fast as possible immediately
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Slow, accurate practice supports technique and timing.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What should a student do if repeated playing causes persistent pain?
options: Stop forcing the movement and seek qualified guidance if pain persists
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Persistent pain should not be ignored; technique and rest matter.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: Which are the three common parts of a tala structure taught in basic theory?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Laghu, drutam, and anudrutam are basic tala angas.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: Which system uses the terms Sa, Ri, Ga, Ma, Pa, Da, Ni for notes?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: These are the standard Carnatic swara syllables.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What is the difference between raga and tala?
options: Raga and tala are the same thing
Raga organizes melody; tala organizes rhythmic time
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Raga and tala are complementary but distinct musical frameworks.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: Why is it useful for percussion students to learn basic raga and composition structure?
options: It means they never need tala practice
It helps them accompany sensitively and anticipate musical sections
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Understanding the music helps percussionists coordinate with the main artist.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What does 'kalapramanam' refer to broadly?
options: The tempo or speed maintained in a performance
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Kalapramanam refers to the maintained tempo.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What is the role of the tala cycle in improvisation?
options: It provides a rhythmic framework for phrases and their resolution
It removes the need for timing
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Tala helps organize rhythmic improvisation and its landing points.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What does 'samam' generally mean in tala counting?
options: The starting point of the tala cycle
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.why: Samam is commonly used for the beginning/reference point of a tala cycle.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Percussion.q: What is a 'vishama eduppu'?
options: A musical entry point that is offset from samam

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: A kriti is a major compositional form in Carnatic music.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Which option best answers this: Which are the usual main sections of a kriti?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Many kritis are structured with Pallavi, Anupallavi, and Charanam.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Choose the correct answer: What is 'Alapana'?
options: Improvisational exploration of a raga without fixed tala
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Alapana explores a raga melodically without a fixed rhythmic cycle.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Carnatic vocal practice: What is 'Neraval' in Carnatic performance?
options: Improvisation on a selected line of a composition
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Neraval develops melodic and rhythmic variations around a chosen line.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Which option best answers this: What is 'Kalpana Swarams'?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Kalpana swarams are improvised note passages.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Choose the correct answer: What is a 'Ragam-Tanam-Pallavi' (RTP)?
options: An advanced concert format featuring raga, tanam, and pallavi improvisation
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: RTP is a major improvisational format in Carnatic concerts.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Carnatic vocal practice: What is 'Tanam' commonly associated with?
options: Rhythmic-melodic improvisation, often using syllables such as 'ananta'
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Tanam is a rhythmic-melodic improvisational section, often using characteristic syllables.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Which option best answers this: Which of these is one of the seven basic talas in the Carnatic system?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Adi tala is widely used in Carnatic music.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Choose the correct answer: What is the common anga pattern of Adi tala?
options: One anudrutam and one laghu only
One laghu followed by two drutams
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Adi tala is commonly structured as a chatusra-jati laghu followed by two drutams.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Carnatic vocal practice: In chatusra-jati Adi tala, how many aksharas are counted in the usual cycle?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: The standard chatusra-jati Adi tala cycle has eight aksharas.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Which option best answers this: What does 'Laya' mean in music?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Laya refers to tempo or temporal flow.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Choose the correct answer: What is a 'Korvai' commonly understood as?
options: A structured rhythmic phrase or sequence, often repeated to conclude a section
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Korvais are structured rhythmic patterns, often used as cadential phrases.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Carnatic vocal practice: Which percussion instrument is most commonly associated with Carnatic concerts?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: The mridangam is the principal percussion instrument in many Carnatic concerts.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Which option best answers this: Why is a pitch reference important for a Carnatic vocalist?
options: It removes the need for breathing
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Consistent sruti alignment is central to vocal practice.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Choose the correct answer: What is the usual purpose of Sarali Varisai exercises?
options: To learn basic swara patterns and develop foundational control
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Sarali varisai helps beginners learn basic note patterns.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Carnatic vocal practice: What are Janta Varisai exercises designed to practise?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Janta varisai uses repeated swaras to build control and clarity.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Which option best answers this: What is the main focus of Alankaram exercises?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Alankaram exercises combine note patterns with tala structures.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Choose the correct answer: Why do vocalists practise at different speeds (kalams)?
options: To develop accuracy, control, and rhythmic steadiness
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Practising multiple speeds develops control and precision.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Carnatic vocal practice: What is the purpose of voice warm-ups before singing?
options: To increase volume at any cost
To force the highest notes immediately
To prepare the voice gradually for singing
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Gentle warm-ups prepare the voice and help reduce strain.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Which option best answers this: Which practice is generally safest for vocal development?
options: Gradual, comfortable practice without forcing the voice
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Gradual practice supports development; pain or persistent hoarseness warrants rest and professional advice.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Choose the correct answer: What does 'Manodharma' refer to in Carnatic music?
options: Creative improvisation within the musical tradition
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Manodharma is the creative, improvisational aspect of performance.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Carnatic vocal practice: Which raga is traditionally associated with the notes Sa, Ri2, Ga3, Ma1, Pa, Da2, Ni3 in its full scale?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Shankarabharanam is a major melakarta raga with that commonly taught scale.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Which option best answers this: Which raga is commonly taught to beginners through foundational lessons in many Carnatic music schools?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Mayamalavagowla is widely used for early foundational lessons, though teaching practice varies.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Choose the correct answer: Which raga is commonly described as pentatonic, using five notes in ascent and descent in its basic form?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Mohanam is a well-known audava (five-note) raga in ascent and descent.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Carnatic vocal practice: What is a 'Melakarta' raga?
options: One of the 72 parent ragas in the Carnatic system
Any raga with five notes only
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: The standard Carnatic melakarta scheme contains 72 parent ragas.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Which option best answers this: What is a 'Janya raga'?
options: A raga derived from a melakarta parent raga
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Janya ragas are derived from parent melakarta ragas.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Choose the correct answer: What is the usual role of the violin in a Carnatic vocal concert?
options: To keep the primary tala with cymbals
To accompany and respond to the vocalist melodically
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: The violin commonly supports the vocalist and echoes melodic phrases.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Carnatic vocal practice: What is a 'Tani Avartanam'?
options: A percussion solo within a rhythmic cycle
A solo raga exposition without tala
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Tani avartanam is the percussion solo segment of a concert.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Which option best answers this: What is a 'Mangalam' often used for in a concert?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Mangalam often concludes a concert with an auspicious benediction.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Choose the correct answer: What is the role of a concert's 'Varnam' in many performances?
options: A composition that develops technical and melodic skills and may open a concert
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Varnams are important learning and performance compositions, often used to begin concerts.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Carnatic vocal practice: What does 'Bhava' refer to in musical expression?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Bhava refers to expressive feeling conveyed through music.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Which option best answers this: What does 'Sahitya' mean in a vocal composition?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Sahitya is the lyrical text of a composition.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Choose the correct answer: Which saint-composer is associated with the composition 'Jagadananda Karaka'?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: 'Jagadananda Karaka' is one of Tyagaraja's Pancharatna kritis.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Carnatic vocal practice: The Pancharatna Kritis are associated with which composer?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Tyagaraja's Pancharatna Kritis are five celebrated compositions.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Which option best answers this: Which composer is associated with the Navagraha kritis?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Dikshitar composed a well-known set of Navagraha kritis.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Choose the correct answer: Who composed 'Vatapi Ganapatim'?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: 'Vatapi Ganapatim' is attributed to Muthuswami Dikshitar.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Carnatic vocal practice: Which composer is associated with the kriti 'Brochevarevarura'?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: 'Brochevarevarura' is a well-known composition attributed to Tyagaraja.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Which option best answers this: Which composer is associated with 'Bhavayami Gopalabalam'?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: The commonly performed composition 'Bhavayami Gopalabalam' is associated with Annamacharya; performance and attribution contexts can vary.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Choose the correct answer: What is the usual number of melakarta ragas in the standard Carnatic system?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: The standard melakarta system comprises 72 parent ragas.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Carnatic vocal practice: What is a 'Vadi' or equivalent dominant-note idea most closely related to in broad raga theory?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: The term vadi is more prominent in Hindustani theory; in broad comparative discussion it means a dominant note.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Which option best answers this: What does 'Sangati' refer to in a kriti performance?
options: A melodic variation of a line
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Sangatis are melodic variations developed for a composition line.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Choose the correct answer: What does 'Akshara kala' refer to in tala context?
options: The time value or unit associated with a tala count
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Akshara kala relates to the temporal unit/counting framework in tala.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Carnatic vocal practice: Which is the common seven-swara solfege sequence in Carnatic music?
options: Do Re Mi Fa Sol La Ti
Sa Ri Ga Ma Pa Da Ni
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Carnatic swara syllables are Sa, Ri, Ga, Ma, Pa, Da and Ni.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Which option best answers this: What is the main difference between a raga's arohana and avarohana?
options: They are names for concert venues
Arohana is ascending and avarohana is descending
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Arohana describes ascent; avarohana describes descent.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Choose the correct answer: What is 'Sruti bedham' commonly associated with?
options: Shifting the perceived tonic to reveal another tonal framework
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Sruti bedham is a technique of shifting the tonic perception to reveal another scale/raga framework.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Carnatic vocal practice: What is a practical benefit of listening to well-trained Carnatic vocal performances?
options: It helps develop listening, raga recognition, and musical phrasing
It changes the vocal range instantly
It removes the need for practice
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Focused listening can strengthen musical awareness when paired with practice.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Which option best answers this: Why should a student learn tala while learning a composition?
options: To eliminate the need for a teacher
To keep the composition rhythmically organized
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Tala supports rhythmic accuracy and coordination.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Choose the correct answer: What is a useful way to practise a difficult musical phrase?
options: Slow it down, repeat accurately, then gradually increase speed
Sing it as fast as possible immediately
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Slow, accurate repetition helps build reliable technique.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Carnatic vocal practice: What is the purpose of recording one's practice occasionally?
options: To review pitch, rhythm, clarity, and progress
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Recordings can help students assess their own practice.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Which option best answers this: Which is a healthy approach to improving vocal range?
options: Develop range gradually without forcing notes
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Gradual, comfortable work is safer than forcing range.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Choose the correct answer: What should a student do if singing causes persistent pain or hoarseness?
options: Stop forcing the voice and seek qualified advice if it persists
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Persistent pain or hoarseness should not be ignored.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Carnatic vocal practice: What is the name for the tonic note chosen by a singer for a performance?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Adhara shadja is the chosen tonic reference.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Which option best answers this: Which device is often used by students to provide a steady pitch drone?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: An electronic tambura or shruti box can provide a drone.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Choose the correct answer: What is a 'Varnam' commonly used for in music training?
options: To develop voice, raga familiarity, and rhythmic control
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Varnam practice develops several core performance skills.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Carnatic vocal practice: What does 'Charanam' usually refer to in a kriti?
options: A principal stanza or section following earlier sections
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Charanam is a main section of many kritis.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Which option best answers this: What is a 'Pallavi' in a kriti?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Pallavi is the opening/refrain section in many compositions.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Choose the correct answer: What is 'Anga' in tala terminology?
options: A constituent part of a tala
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Angas are structural components used in tala descriptions.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Carnatic vocal practice: Which hand action is commonly used to mark tala?
options: Clapping and finger counts, according to the tala
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Carnatic tala is often marked with claps, waves, and finger counts.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Which option best answers this: Which raga is commonly associated with the composition 'Endaro Mahanubhavulu'?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: The Pancharatna kriti 'Endaro Mahanubhavulu' is in Sri raga.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Choose the correct answer: Which raga is commonly associated with the kriti 'Vatapi Ganapatim'?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: 'Vatapi Ganapatim' is commonly rendered in Hamsadhwani.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Carnatic vocal practice: Which raga is associated with Tyagaraja's 'Nagumomu Ganaleni' in the commonly accepted version?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: 'Nagumomu Ganaleni' is commonly associated with Abheri.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Which option best answers this: What is 'Sruti shuddham'?
options: Accuracy in maintaining the pitch reference
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Sruti shuddham means maintaining accurate pitch alignment.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Choose the correct answer: What is the role of the ghatam in a Carnatic concert?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: The ghatam is a clay-pot percussion instrument.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Carnatic vocal practice: Which instrument is commonly used as a drone alongside Carnatic vocal music?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: The tambura provides the drone.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Which option best answers this: What is the purpose of practising gamakas carefully?
options: To render the raga's characteristic melodic nuances accurately
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Gamakas are central to the identity and expression of many ragas.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Choose the correct answer: What should a vocalist prioritize when learning new lyrics?
options: Correct pronunciation, meaning, and alignment with the melody
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Clear sahitya pronunciation and musical alignment support good rendition.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Carnatic vocal practice: Which composer is known for the Tamil composition 'Kurai Ondrum Illai'?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: 'Kurai Ondrum Illai' is attributed to C. Rajagopalachari.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Which option best answers this: Which composer is widely associated with the Tamil kriti 'Enna Tavam Seithanai'?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: 'Enna Tavam Seithanai' is widely associated with Papanasam Sivan.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Choose the correct answer: What is the term for a phrase or motif characteristic of a raga?
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Prayoga refers to characteristic usage or phrase in a raga.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Carnatic vocal practice: What is a 'Jati' in tala classification?
options: The count type of the laghu
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Jati determines the count of the laghu in a tala.

CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.q: Which option best answers this: Why is consistent daily practice useful for a Carnatic vocalist?
options: It eliminates the need for rest
It guarantees perfect performance without effort
It reinforces pitch, rhythm, memory, and vocal coordination
CBSE 12 - Carnatic Vocal.why: Regular, balanced practice reinforces core musical skills.

Hindustani - Melodic.q: What is the central melodic framework in Hindustani classical music called?
Hindustani - Melodic.why: A raga shapes melody through characteristic notes, phrases, and movement.

Hindustani - Melodic.why: Aroha describes the ascent of notes in a raga.

options: Sa, Ri, Ga, Ma, Pa, Da, Ni
Sa, Re, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha, Ni

Hindustani - Melodic.q: What is the main role of Sa during vocal practice?
options: It determines the tala's number of beats

It provides the tonic or pitch reference
Hindustani - Melodic.why: Sa acts as the tonic reference, with the chosen pitch suited to the singer.

Hindustani - Melodic.q: What is a 'pakad' in raga learning?
options: A characteristic melodic phrase associated with a raga
Hindustani - Melodic.why: A pakad is a phrase that helps express or identify a raga's character.

Hindustani - Melodic.q: What does 'raga bhava' refer to?
options: The expressive character or mood of a raga

Hindustani - Melodic.why: Raga bhava refers to the expressive character conveyed by a raga.

Hindustani - Melodic.q: What is a thaat in the Hindustani system?
options: A parent-scale classification used for ragas
Hindustani - Melodic.why: Thaat is a classification framework based on parent-scale patterns.

Hindustani - Melodic.q: How many thaats are in the commonly taught Bhatkhande classification system?
Hindustani - Melodic.why: The Bhatkhande system commonly groups ragas under ten thaats.

Hindustani - Melodic.q: What does 'meend' mean in melodic performance?
options: A glide from one pitch to another
Hindustani - Melodic.why: Meend is a smooth glide between pitches.

Hindustani - Melodic.q: What does 'murki' describe?
Hindustani - Melodic.why: Murki is a quick ornamental turn in a melodic line.

Hindustani - Melodic.q: What is 'andolan' in raga rendition?
options: A slow oscillation around a note
Hindustani - Melodic.why: Andolan is a characteristic slow oscillation around a pitch.

Hindustani - Melodic.q: What does 'kan swar' refer to?
options: A grace note used to ornament a main note
Hindustani - Melodic.why: Kan swar is a grace note that ornaments a main note.

Hindustani - Melodic.q: What is 'gamak' broadly associated with in Hindustani music?
options: A type of melodic ornament or forceful oscillation
Hindustani - Melodic.why: Gamak refers to a melodic ornament, with its exact use depending on context.

Hindustani - Melodic.q: What is 'alap' in Hindustani vocal music?
Hindustani - Melodic.why: Alap develops the raga's melodic character, often without a fixed tala at first.

Hindustani - Melodic.q: What is a 'taan'?
options: A fast melodic passage or run

options: A repeating melodic cycle that supports the rhythmic solo
Hindustani - Percussion.why: A lehra provides a repeating melody over which the tabla soloist develops rhythmic ideas.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: In the context of Hindustani rhythm, What is a gharana in tabla tradition?
options: A lineage or school with characteristic stylistic approaches
Hindustani - Percussion.why: A gharana is a lineage or school associated with particular stylistic features and repertoire.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: In the context of Hindustani rhythm, Why should students learn several thekas?
options: Every tala uses exactly the same pattern
Different talas require different characteristic patterns
Hindustani - Percussion.why: Learning thekas helps students recognize and articulate different rhythmic cycles.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: In the context of Hindustani rhythm, Which is a useful way to improve tala awareness?
options: Clap and count the cycle while listening
Hindustani - Percussion.why: Clapping and counting make the structure of a tala easier to hear and internalize.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: In the context of Hindustani rhythm, What is a metronome useful for in practice?
Hindustani - Percussion.why: A metronome can provide a steady pulse for timing exercises, though musical tala practice is also essential.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: In the context of Hindustani rhythm, Why should students practice with a tanpura or lehra recording when appropriate?
options: To learn to stay coordinated with a musical reference
To make percussion louder by itself
Hindustani - Percussion.why: A musical reference helps the player maintain timing and respond to the performance context.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: In the context of Hindustani rhythm, What is a sensible approach when increasing tempo?
options: Increase gradually while preserving clarity and evenness
Increase immediately to the fastest possible speed
Hindustani - Percussion.why: Gradual tempo increases reinforce clean technique and rhythmic stability.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: In the context of Hindustani rhythm, Why is recording one’s practice helpful?
options: It can reveal timing, tone and consistency issues
Hindustani - Percussion.why: Listening back can help identify uneven strokes, timing drift and areas for improvement.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: In the context of Hindustani rhythm, What should a student do if playing causes persistent pain?
options: Stop and seek qualified guidance about technique and strain
Hindustani - Percussion.why: Persistent pain should not be ignored; rest and qualified advice can help prevent injury.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: Which statement best describes this concept: Which instrument is most strongly associated with percussion accompaniment in Hindustani khayal music?
Hindustani - Percussion.why: Tabla is widely used to accompany khayal and many other Hindustani music forms.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: Which statement best describes this concept: Which two drums make up a standard tabla set?
Hindustani - Percussion.why: The tabla pair consists of the smaller dayan and the larger bayan.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: Which statement best describes this concept: Which drum in a tabla pair is usually played with the right hand?
Hindustani - Percussion.why: The dayan is the smaller, usually wooden drum played mainly with the right hand.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: Which statement best describes this concept: Which tabla drum commonly provides deeper bass tones?
Hindustani - Percussion.why: The bayan is the larger metal or clay drum and produces bass tones.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: Which statement best describes this concept: Which percussion instrument is especially associated with dhrupad accompaniment?
Hindustani - Percussion.why: Pakhawaj is a barrel-shaped drum traditionally associated with dhrupad.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: Which statement best describes this concept: What is the central rhythmic cycle in Hindustani music called?
Hindustani - Percussion.why: A tala is a repeating rhythmic cycle organized into beats and sections.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: Which statement best describes this concept: What is the standard rhythmic pattern that outlines a tala called?
Hindustani - Percussion.why: Theka is a characteristic sequence of tabla bols that articulates a tala.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: Which statement best describes this concept: What are the spoken syllables used to represent drum strokes called?
Hindustani - Percussion.why: Bols are mnemonic syllables for percussion strokes and patterns.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: Which statement best describes this concept: What does laya refer to in Hindustani rhythm?
Hindustani - Percussion.why: Laya refers to the pace or tempo of musical performance.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: Which statement best describes this concept: What is layakari?
options: Rhythmic variation or play with subdivisions against the beat
Hindustani - Percussion.why: Layakari explores rhythmic relationships and subdivisions within a tala.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: Which statement best describes this concept: What does sam indicate in a tala cycle?
options: The final note of a raga
The first and most important beat of the cycle
Hindustani - Percussion.why: Sam is the cycle’s principal point of arrival, commonly marked by performers.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: Which statement best describes this concept: What is khali in tala structure?
options: An indicated empty or unstressed section, often marked by a wave of the hand
Hindustani - Percussion.why: Khali marks a section conventionally shown with a wave rather than a clap.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: Which statement best describes this concept: What is a tali in tala counting?
options: A clap marking a section of the cycle
Hindustani - Percussion.why: Tali is a clap used to mark a beat or section in tala demonstration.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: Which statement best describes this concept: How many matras are in Teentaal?
Hindustani - Percussion.why: Teentaal is a 16-beat cycle, commonly grouped 4+4+4+4.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: Which statement best describes this concept: How many matras are in Jhaptaal?
Hindustani - Percussion.why: Jhaptaal has 10 beats, commonly grouped 2+3+2+3.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: Which statement best describes this concept: How many matras are in Rupak taal in its common form?
Hindustani - Percussion.why: Rupak is commonly a seven-beat cycle, often grouped 3+2+2.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: Which statement best describes this concept: How many matras are in Ektaal?
Hindustani - Percussion.why: Ektaal is a 12-beat cycle often used in classical vocal and instrumental music.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: Which statement best describes this concept: How many matras are in Dadra taal?
Hindustani - Percussion.why: Dadra is a six-beat cycle, often used in light-classical forms.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: Which statement best describes this concept: How many matras are in Keharwa taal?
Hindustani - Percussion.why: Keharwa is an eight-beat cycle widely used in folk and light music.

Hindustani - Percussion.q: Which statement best describes this concept: How many matras are in Dhamar taal?
Hindustani - Percussion.why: Dhamar taal has 14 beats and is associated with the Dhamar singing tradition.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Hindustani classical vocal music is primarily associated with which region of the Indian subcontinent?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Hindustani classical music developed mainly in North India.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is a raga in Hindustani music?
options: A melodic framework with characteristic rules and phrases
Hindustani - Vocal.why: A raga shapes melody through characteristic notes and movements.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is a tala?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Tala organizes musical time in a repeating cycle.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What does 'swar' refer to?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Swar refers to a musical note.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Which are the seven basic swar names commonly used in Hindustani music?
options: Sa, Re, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha, Ni
Sa, Ri, Ga, Ma, Pa, Da, Ni
Hindustani - Vocal.why: The seven basic swars are Sa, Re, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha and Ni.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is the tonic reference note commonly called?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Sa acts as the tonic reference, with its pitch chosen to suit the singer.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What does 'alap' or 'alapana' generally mean in Hindustani vocal music?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Alap explores the raga's melodic character, often without a fixed tala at the beginning.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is a 'bandish'?
options: A composed musical piece set in a raga and tala
Hindustani - Vocal.why: A bandish is a composition used as a basis for raga presentation.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is the ascending movement of notes in a raga called?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Aroha describes ascending movement.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is the descending movement of notes in a raga called?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Avaroha describes descending movement.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is a 'pakad' in Hindustani music?
options: A characteristic phrase that helps identify a raga
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Pakad is a characteristic melodic phrase associated with a raga.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Which term describes a raga's emotional or expressive character?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Raga bhava refers to the expressive character of a raga.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is a thaat in the Hindustani system?
options: A parent scale used to classify ragas
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Thaat is a classification framework based on parent scales.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: How many thaats are in the commonly taught Bhatkhande classification system?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: The Bhatkhande system commonly classifies ragas under ten thaats.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Which raga is often taught early to beginners and is associated with the Kalyan thaat?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Yaman is commonly taught early and is associated with Kalyan thaat.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Which raga is commonly associated with the Bhairav thaat?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Bhairav is the namesake raga of Bhairav thaat.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Which raga is commonly associated with the Kafi thaat?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Kafi is associated with the Kafi thaat.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What does 'vadi' refer to in Hindustani raga theory?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Vadi is traditionally described as a prominent note in a raga.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What does 'samvadi' refer to?
options: A note considered second in prominence in relation to the vadi
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Samvadi is a note traditionally described as second in prominence to the vadi.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What does 'vivadi swar' refer to broadly?
options: A note treated as dissonant or restricted in a raga context
The tonic note in every raga
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Vivadi refers to a note considered dissonant or specially treated in a raga context.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Which Hindustani vocal form is known for elaborate raga development and a generally slow, expansive presentation?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Dhrupad is a major classical vocal form known for extensive raga development.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Which vocal form is especially associated with flexible melodic elaboration and bol-taan?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Khayal allows extensive improvisation, including taan and bol-based elaboration.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Which Hindustani vocal form is often associated with romantic or devotional expression and lighter treatment of raga grammar?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Thumri is known for expressive, lyrical treatment.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Which form commonly uses syllables such as 'tanom' or 'dir dir' rather than ordinary lyrical text?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Tarana uses rhythmic syllables as part of its text.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Which form is often associated with a fast, agile style and Punjabi folk influence?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Tappa is known for quick, intricate melodic turns and Punjabi roots.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Which devotional vocal form is commonly sung in praise of a deity?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: A bhajan is a devotional song.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Which form is traditionally associated with the Dhamar tala and Holi themes?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Dhamar is associated with a form and tala linked traditionally with Holi themes.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is a 'thumri' singer often expected to emphasize?
options: Expressive interpretation of the lyrics and melodic nuances
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Thumri emphasizes expressive lyric interpretation and melodic nuance.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is a 'taan'?
options: A fast melodic passage or run
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Taan is a rapid melodic passage used in improvisation.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is 'bol-taan'?
options: Taan patterns sung using words or syllables from the bandish
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Bol-taan combines melodic runs with syllables from the composition.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is 'sargam' singing?
options: Singing melodic passages using note names
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Sargam uses note syllables such as Sa, Re, Ga, Ma.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What does 'layakari' refer to?
options: Creative rhythmic play against the underlying pulse or tala
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Layakari involves rhythmic variation and play.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is a 'tihai'?
options: A vocal form with no rhythm
A phrase repeated three times to arrive at a rhythmic point
Hindustani - Vocal.why: A tihai repeats a phrase three times, commonly resolving at sam.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is 'bol-alap' in khayal?
options: Raga elaboration using the words of the composition
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Bol-alap uses the composition's words to elaborate the raga.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is 'meend'?
options: A glide from one pitch to another
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Meend is a smooth glide between pitches.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is 'gamak' in Hindustani vocal music?
options: A forceful or oscillatory melodic ornament, depending on context
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Gamak refers to a type of melodic ornament, with meaning depending on context.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What does 'murki' describe?
options: A quick, delicate cluster of notes or ornament
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Murki is a quick, ornamental melodic turn.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is 'kan swar'?
options: A grace note approached briefly from another note
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Kan swar is a grace note used to ornament a main note.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What does 'andolan' refer to in raga rendition?
options: A slow oscillation around a note
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Andolan is a characteristic slow oscillation around a pitch.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Which instrument most commonly accompanies Hindustani classical vocal music rhythmically?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Tabla is a common rhythmic accompaniment instrument in Hindustani vocal concerts.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is 'theka'?
options: A characteristic pattern of tabla bols that outlines a tala
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Theka is the recognizable pattern used to articulate a tala on tabla.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is 'sam' in Hindustani tala?
options: The first and often most important beat of the cycle
The highest note of a raga
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Sam is the cycle's main point of arrival, usually its first beat.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Which tala is commonly counted in 16 matras?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Teentaal has 16 matras.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: How many matras are in Dadra tala in its common form?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Dadra tala commonly has six matras.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: How many matras are in Keharwa tala in its common form?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Keharwa tala commonly has eight matras.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: How many matras are in Rupak tala in its common Hindustani form?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Rupak tala commonly has seven matras.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is 'matra' in Hindustani tala?
options: A beat or unit of time within the rhythmic cycle
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Matra is a unit of time in a tala cycle.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is the purpose of practising alankars?
options: To develop control over note patterns and melodic movement
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Alankar exercises help develop note control and melodic fluency.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Why is a tanpura or electronic tanpura used during vocal practice?
options: To provide a stable drone and pitch reference
Hindustani - Vocal.why: The tanpura provides a continuous tonal reference.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is a sensible approach to increasing vocal range?
options: Practise gradually without forcing the voice
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Gradual, comfortable practice helps reduce vocal strain.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Why is breath management important in Hindustani singing?
options: It determines the raga's parent scale
It removes the need for rhythm
It supports sustained phrases and controlled expression
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Breath management supports phrasing and vocal control.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What should a singer do if persistent hoarseness or pain occurs?
options: Stop forcing the voice and seek qualified advice if it persists
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Persistent vocal symptoms should not be ignored.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is the benefit of recording one's practice?
options: To eliminate the need to listen
To make the voice louder automatically
To review pitch, rhythm, clarity, and progress
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Recordings can help assess progress and identify areas to improve.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Who is widely known as a major figure in the modern systematization of Hindustani music theory and thaat classification?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Bhatkhande played a major role in systematizing Hindustani music theory.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Which musicologist is known for a major contribution to Hindustani music education and institutions in the early 20th century?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Paluskar helped establish modern music education institutions and promote classical music.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Which gharana is strongly associated with the city of Jaipur?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Jaipur-Atrauli is a prominent Hindustani vocal gharana.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Which gharana is known for emphasis on swara purity and sustained note development?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Kirana gayaki is often associated with careful swara intonation and sustained notes.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Which gharana is historically associated with the Agra region and a distinctive dhrupad-influenced khayal style?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Agra gharana is known for its distinctive khayal style and historical dhrupad influence.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Tansen is traditionally associated with the court of which Mughal emperor?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Tansen is traditionally associated with Emperor Akbar's court.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Which term refers to a musical lineage or school in Hindustani classical music?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: A gharana is a lineage or stylistic school.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is the main purpose of a thaat in Hindustani music?
options: To classify ragas through parent-scale patterns
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Thaats provide a parent-scale classification framework.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is the broad difference between raga and thaat?
options: A thaat is a percussion solo
A raga is a melodic framework; a thaat is a parent-scale classification
A raga is only a rhythm
Hindustani - Vocal.why: A raga has characteristic melodic behavior, while a thaat classifies by scale.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is 'shruti' often used to refer to in Indian classical music?
options: Subtle pitch intervals or the pitch reference, depending on context
Hindustani - Vocal.why: The term has related meanings in Indian music theory and practice.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What does 'vilambit laya' mean?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Vilambit means slow tempo.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What does 'drut laya' mean?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Drut means fast tempo.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What does 'madhya laya' mean?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Madhya laya refers to a medium tempo.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is a 'saptak'?
options: An octave or group of seven swar positions
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Saptak refers to an octave/group of seven swar positions.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is 'madhyam' in the seven-swar system?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Madhyam is the swar Ma.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Which swar is commonly treated as fixed in Hindustani music?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Sa and Pa are generally treated as achal (fixed) swars in the common system.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is a komal swar?
options: A flattened form of a note where applicable
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Komal denotes a lowered form of a swar.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is a tivra swar in the common Hindustani system?
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Ma is the swar commonly described as tivra in Hindustani theory.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What should a student listen for when learning a new raga?
options: Its characteristic phrases, note treatment, and mood
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Listening for phrases and note treatment supports raga understanding.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Why is it useful to learn a bandish phrase by phrase?
options: It eliminates the need to learn the raga
It helps accuracy of melody, words, and rhythm
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Phrase-by-phrase learning supports musical and textual accuracy.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: Which practice best supports accurate intonation?
options: Sing with a stable drone and check notes carefully
Change Sa frequently during the same exercise
Sing only as loudly as possible
Hindustani - Vocal.why: A steady drone helps the singer check pitch.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is a good way to learn a difficult taan?
options: Practise slowly and accurately, then increase speed gradually
Sing it as fast as possible from the start
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Gradual practice supports accuracy and speed.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What does attentive listening to different gharana performances help reveal?
options: Different stylistic approaches to raga interpretation
The exact price of the tanpura
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Different gharanas may emphasize different stylistic approaches.

Hindustani - Vocal.q: What is an appropriate goal for a beginner learning improvisation?
options: Develop clear, raga-appropriate phrases before attempting complexity
Hindustani - Vocal.why: Clear, appropriate phrasing is a strong foundation for improvisation.

Hindustani - Vocal.why: Hindustani classical music developed mainly in North India.
